themes_detail.label: Emergency Response Surge
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, up 380% from a 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden cluster of incidents requiring immediate official intervention in the district.
evidence: 3 Emergency Response Team complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.91)
Statistically significant spike indicates acute disturbance, not seasonal pattern
Timing aligns with recent hit-and-run fatality (April 17) and car meetup incident (April 19) reported by local media
reporting_angles: What specific incidents triggered ERT calls this week? Interview NYPD or fire department
Is the car meetup and hit-and-run creating neighborhood safety anxiety? Survey residents

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Posting complaints jumped to 17 LAST WEEK, a 2620% spike above the 0.6 weekly average, suggesting coordinated campaign graffiti, political posters, or unauthorized commercial advertising saturating the district.
evidence: 17 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 16.5)
Magnitude of spike (2620%) suggests concentrated event rather than gradual trend
No Reddit or CB discussion yet, indicating potential underreporting
reporting_angles: Canvas neighborhoods to identify what's being posted—political, gang tags, or commercial?
Are repeat locations (transit hubs, storefronts) being targeted? Map cluster

themes_detail.label: Park Disturbances and Rule Violations
themes_detail.summary: Park-related complaints clustered 2 weeks ago: Noise in Parks up 7100% (9 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline), Unleashed Dog complaints up 700% (5 vs. 0.6), and Park Rule Violations up 700% (3 vs. 0.4), indicating simultaneous breakdown of park order and enforcement.
evidence: 9 park noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 26.84, highest severity)
5 unleashed dog complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.29)
3 park rule violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
Convergence of three distinct complaint types suggests systemic park safety/management issue
reporting_angles: Visit parks (Fresh Pond, Forest Park, others) with 311 complaint maps; identify hotspots and interview users
Interview Parks Dept about staffing, enforcement, recent incidents; cross-reference with police incident data
Talk to community board about long-standing park upgrade requests (budget data shows repeated park reconstruction requests)

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food Poisoning complaints tripled to 3 THREE WEEKS AGO (up 300% from 0.8 weekly average), signaling potential localized food handling or restaurant hygiene issue requiring health investigation.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.2)
300% spike magnitude suggests cluster, not random incidents
No follow-up in recent data; unclear if resolved or complaints stopped being filed
reporting_angles: FOIL Department of Health inspection records to identify cited establishments in spike window
Contact complainants to determine common venue or food type
Ask health dept: were complaints investigated and resolved? Any ongoing closure orders?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints jumped to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 833% from a 0.8 weekly average, indicating sudden street vending activity, illegal cart placement, or complaint surge regarding food/goods vendors in the district.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.74)
833% increase suggests either new vendor activity or organized enforcement crackdown
Timing may correlate with warm weather and street activity ramp-up
reporting_angles: Identify where complaints are concentrated: transit stations, commercial strips, residential blocks?
Interview street vendors and local business owners about enforcement intensity
Request DOE sidewalk vending permit data to see if new licenses issued recently
